# Skills

<!-- Generated by skills/core/scripts/dev_docs.py from skills/core/shared/help.json and the skill/agent frontmatter. Do not edit by hand: edit the catalog and run `dev_docs.py build`. -->

Every skill is invoked as `/dev-kit:<name>`. Not sure which one? `/dev-kit:help <your question>`.

## Start and orientation

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`start`](#start) | Entry point: starts a new project, adopts an existing codebase (feature, maintenance or import mode) or resumes, and routes to the next skill. |
| [`help`](#help) | Help inside Claude Code: what to do next, how each skill works, recipes and concepts. |
| [`interview`](#interview) | Exhaustive requirements interview in 10 blocks; everything goes to .dev/brief.md with the autonomy policy. |
| [`status`](#status) | Read-only dashboard: lifecycle phase and step, next release, milestones, gates, scores, issues, preview, production drift, cost so far. |
| [`board`](#board) | Live board in the browser, laid out like the flow diagram (docs/dev-kit-flow.svg): its tabs are the lanes - conception, planning, construction in two (milestones and releases) and stable - plus a Map with all five lanes at once, and it opens on the lane where the project is. Each screen fits the window without scrolling: on top the lane's steps as a flow, coloured by who does them (yours in yellow, agents in orange, delivery in green, gates in red), with where the project is, what runs and what waits on you; below, blocks of the same size, where what does not fit opens with "See all". Conception shows its documents, the PRD and design reviews, decisions and facts, and scope changes; planning the roadmap by release, the backlog and the plan review, with a screen of its own to replan by dragging tasks, issues and milestones; milestones the milestone picked (grouped by release) with its stages, the task board in columns of equal height or its QA rounds, and burndown, velocity and gates in a Metrics modal; releases the release picked with its stages (checks, audit, review, your approval, production, released) and its numbers, milestones, blockers and documents; stable the project totals, production, the health check, release flags, release checks and releases. "Needs you" is a button in the top bar that turns red (and rings once) when something waits, with a badge on the lane and on the step it belongs to; it opens a drawer with every item and its buttons (Approve and Reject for a release). Requests and activity are drawers too. Every link to a document of .dev/ opens it formatted in a side panel. Buttons ask Claude Code for work (run the next step, new issue, answer a question, a plan draft) and start it in the session that opened the board; the Autopilot switch in the top bar runs /dev-kit:autopilot from the board, one milestone per run, until a release waits for your approval, waiting on Needs you when only your decisions are left; hovering Live lists what is running; light or dark, English or Portuguese; local, shared on your network with an access link, or behind your reverse proxy. |
| [`worker`](#worker) | Runs the requests you queued on the board (run a command, new issue, answer a question, plan draft, release approval or rejection) in this Claude Code session, one at a time; questions that would stop the run go to the board with answers to pick. |
| [`settings`](#settings) | Shows and changes the project's settings in plain words: autonomy, quality bar, rounds, reuse, checks, deploys, tips, status line and notifications. |

## Specify

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`prd`](#prd) | Product requirements with user stories and numbered acceptance criteria (AC-n). |
| [`architecture`](#architecture) | Stack, repository layout, data model, contracts, environments, deploy commands and ADRs. |
| [`ux`](#ux) | Information architecture, journeys, every screen state, forms and microcopy guide. |
| [`ui`](#ui) | Design tokens, components with states, and a spec for every screen (responsive, dark mode, accessibility). |
| [`plan`](#plan) | Milestones M1..Mn and small vertical-slice tasks T-xxx with dependencies, ACs and files. |
| [`review`](#review) | Scored independent review (0-100, with cut-off) of the PRD, design, plan or docs, looping until it passes. |

## Build

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`autopilot`](#autopilot) | Drives the build on its own: conception and planning, then milestone after milestone and the next release, until the project is stable; pauses follow your autonomy settings. |
| [`implement`](#implement) | Implements ready tasks test-first, full suite, one commit per task; hotfix lane first. |
| [`test`](#test) | Test strategy and test writing: plan, missing tests for a task or path, flaky tests. |

## Quality

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`qa`](#qa) | Milestone gate: auditors in parallel, 0-100 score per dimension, fix tasks until the cut-off is met. |
| [`usability`](#usability) | Whole-product audit of usability, accessibility, visuals and copy, with score and fix tasks. |

## Bugs, changes and what is pending

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`issue`](#issue) | Report a bug, improvement or scope change in plain words; the kit classifies and routes it without breaking the milestone cadence. |
| [`backlog`](#backlog) | Everything pending: hotfix, issue queue, next buffer, tasks, parked questions, deferred findings, deploys. |

## Ship

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`deploy`](#deploy) | Production deploy of an approved milestone or release: preflight, backup, dry-run, install, migrations, smoke checks. |
| [`docs`](#docs) | Project documentation from the artifacts and code: README, user guide, API reference, CHANGELOG. |
| [`release`](#release) | Ships the next release (the milestones closed since the last release, or the next planned release): audits, the release review and your approve/reject decision for a planned release, then version, CHANGELOG, tag, production deploy and the release record; patch releases for hotfixes. |

## Observe

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`costs`](#costs) | Token usage and estimated US$ (API-equivalent) per stage, agent, model or session; CSV of tokens. |
| [`feedback`](#feedback) | Evaluation of the session: grade per stage with reasons, what worked and failed, suggestions for the kit. |

### start

Entry point: starts a new project, adopts an existing codebase (feature, maintenance or import mode) or resumes, and routes to the next skill.

**When:** First command in any project, and whenever you come back and want to know where things stopped.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:start [project idea or goal, or empty to resume]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `idea` | a project idea starts the interview; in an existing codebase it is the goal of the change, after the onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline) |
| `(empty)` | resume: reconcile with git and route |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:start a personal expense tracker`: new project: git init if needed, then the interview
- `/dev-kit:start add CSV export to the reports page`: existing codebase without .dev/: onboarding (baseline tag, discovery, test baseline, retroactive ADRs), then a short interview about the change
- `/dev-kit:start`: resume where the project stopped

**Produces:** routing only; starts a session in the log

**Related:** [`interview`](#interview), [`status`](#status), [`help`](#help)

### help

Help inside Claude Code: what to do next, how each skill works, recipes and concepts.

**When:** Whenever you are unsure which skill to use or what something means.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:help [skill | question | agents | concept]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `(empty)` | next steps for this project and the skill map |
| `skill` | card of one skill |
| `question` | the recipe or concept that answers it |
| `agents` | the agents and who calls them |
| `concept` | a term such as gate, buffer or baseline: its definition |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:help`: what to do now
- `/dev-kit:help issue`: how to report bugs and improvements
- `/dev-kit:help how do I run it overnight?`: the unattended recipe

**Produces:** nothing (read-only)

**Related:** [`status`](#status), [`backlog`](#backlog)

### interview

Exhaustive requirements interview in 10 blocks; everything goes to .dev/brief.md with the autonomy policy.

**When:** Beginning of a project (start calls it), or later to answer questions the kit parked.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:interview [initial idea | --gaps | --express]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `idea` | initial idea |
| `--express` | one round with the 4 most important questions |
| `--gaps` | answer open and parked questions |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:interview --gaps`: resolve what the kit parked or assumed

**Produces:** .dev/brief.md, .dev/decisions.md, autonomy and quality settings

**Related:** [`start`](#start), [`prd`](#prd), [`autopilot`](#autopilot)

### status

Read-only dashboard: lifecycle phase and step, next release, milestones, gates, scores, issues, preview, production drift, cost so far.

**When:** Any time you want a quick picture of the project.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:status [--json]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--json` | machine-readable state |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:status`: where the project stands

**Produces:** nothing (read-only)

**Related:** [`backlog`](#backlog), [`costs`](#costs), [`help`](#help)

### board

Live board in the browser, laid out like the flow diagram (docs/dev-kit-flow.svg): its tabs are the lanes - conception, planning, construction in two (milestones and releases) and stable - plus a Map with all five lanes at once, and it opens on the lane where the project is. Each screen fits the window without scrolling: on top the lane's steps as a flow, coloured by who does them (yours in yellow, agents in orange, delivery in green, gates in red), with where the project is, what runs and what waits on you; below, blocks of the same size, where what does not fit opens with "See all". Conception shows its documents, the PRD and design reviews, decisions and facts, and scope changes; planning the roadmap by release, the backlog and the plan review, with a screen of its own to replan by dragging tasks, issues and milestones; milestones the milestone picked (grouped by release) with its stages, the task board in columns of equal height or its QA rounds, and burndown, velocity and gates in a Metrics modal; releases the release picked with its stages (checks, audit, review, your approval, production, released) and its numbers, milestones, blockers and documents; stable the project totals, production, the health check, release flags, release checks and releases. "Needs you" is a button in the top bar that turns red (and rings once) when something waits, with a badge on the lane and on the step it belongs to; it opens a drawer with every item and its buttons (Approve and Reject for a release). Requests and activity are drawers too. Every link to a document of .dev/ opens it formatted in a side panel. Buttons ask Claude Code for work (run the next step, new issue, answer a question, a plan draft) and start it in the session that opened the board; the Autopilot switch in the top bar runs /dev-kit:autopilot from the board, one milestone per run, until a release waits for your approval, waiting on Needs you when only your decisions are left; hovering Live lists what is running; light or dark, English or Portuguese; local, shared on your network with an access link, or behind your reverse proxy.

**When:** When you want to watch the project visually or drive it from the browser, e.g. away from the console; it updates by itself.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:board [stop | status | --open | --no-open | --port N | --host IP | --trusted-host NAME | --idle-min N | --actions on|off]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `(empty)` | start the local server (or reuse the running one) and open the default browser |
| `stop` | stop the server (the page also has a Stop server button) |
| `status` | whether it is running, its URL and PID |
| `--open | --no-open | --port N` | force a new tab, do not open a tab, preferred port (default 8765) |
| `--host IP` | listen address (default 127.0.0.1); 0.0.0.0 shares the board on the network, opened only with the access link it prints |
| `--idle-min N` | stop after N minutes with no open tab (default 120; 0 = never) |
| `--trusted-host NAME` | host name of your reverse proxy in front of the board (remembered for the project; none forgets it) |
| `--actions on|off` | let the page queue requests to Claude Code (on by default; off makes the board show the project only) |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:board`: open the board; calling it again does not start a second server or a second tab
- `/dev-kit:board --host 0.0.0.0`: share it on your network (phone, another computer) with a private access link
- `/dev-kit:board stop`: stop the board server

**Produces:** nothing in the project by itself (requests are run by /dev-kit:worker: in the session that listens, or in a headless session the board starts itself when none does); its own files in .dev/run/

**Related:** [`worker`](#worker), [`status`](#status), [`backlog`](#backlog), [`costs`](#costs)

### worker

Runs the requests you queued on the board (run a command, new issue, answer a question, plan draft, release approval or rejection) in this Claude Code session, one at a time; questions that would stop the run go to the board with answers to pick.

**When:** It starts by itself, each time a request arrives: in the session that opened the board with /dev-kit:board, or, when no session listens, in a headless session the board starts (autonomy.board_executor). Run it by hand in another session only when the board says it cannot start Claude Code.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:worker `

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `(empty)` | run every request waiting on the board, in order, until none is left or the queue is paused |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:worker`: run what you asked for on the board

**Produces:** whatever each request does (commits, issues, plan changes); the request's result on the board

**Related:** [`board`](#board), [`issue`](#issue), [`plan`](#plan)

### prd

Product requirements with user stories and numbered acceptance criteria (AC-n).

**When:** After the interview, or to revise requirements when scope changes.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:prd [focus or change request]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `focus or change request` | what to (re)write |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:prd`: write the PRD from the brief
- `/dev-kit:prd add CSV export of reports`: revise for a scope change

**Produces:** .dev/prd.md

**Related:** [`review`](#review), [`architecture`](#architecture), [`issue`](#issue)

### architecture

Stack, repository layout, data model, contracts, environments, deploy commands and ADRs.

**When:** After the PRD passes review, or when a structural decision must be revisited.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:architecture [constraints or 'review']`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `constraints` | extra constraints to respect |
| `review` | revisit the current architecture |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:architecture`: decide and document the architecture

**Produces:** .dev/architecture.md, .dev/decisions.md

**Related:** [`prd`](#prd), [`ux`](#ux), [`plan`](#plan)

### ux

Information architecture, journeys, every screen state, forms and microcopy guide.

**When:** Products with a UI, after architecture, or to redesign a flow.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:ux [flow, persona or screen to (re)design]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `flow, persona or screen` | what to (re)design |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:ux`: design all flows
- `/dev-kit:ux checkout`: redesign one flow

**Produces:** .dev/design/ux-flows.md

**Related:** [`ui`](#ui), [`review`](#review)

### ui

Design tokens, components with states, and a spec for every screen (responsive, dark mode, accessibility).

**When:** After ux, or to (re)specify a screen or component.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:ui [screen id, component or 'tokens']`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `screen, component or tokens` | what to (re)specify |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:ui`: full UI spec
- `/dev-kit:ui tokens`: only the design tokens

**Produces:** .dev/design/ui-spec.md

**Related:** [`ux`](#ux), [`review`](#review)

### plan

Milestones M1..Mn and small vertical-slice tasks T-xxx with dependencies, ACs and files.

**When:** After design (or architecture for UI-less products), and to replan remaining work.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:plan [milestone focus | 'replan' | --annotate-risk | --annotate-exit]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `milestone focus` | plan one area |
| `replan` | rewrite only todo tasks of future milestones |
| `--annotate-risk` | add the risk fields to tasks already planned, without replanning |
| `--annotate-exit` | propose an exit_check for each open milestone of an older plan |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:plan`: plan the whole build
- `/dev-kit:plan replan`: after a scope change
- `/dev-kit:plan --annotate-risk`: existing plan, before the next milestone

**Produces:** .dev/plan.md synced into .dev/state.json

**Related:** [`review`](#review), [`implement`](#implement), [`autopilot`](#autopilot)

### review

Scored independent review (0-100, with cut-off) of the PRD, design, plan or docs, looping until it passes.

**When:** Before implementation (prd, design, plan) and before release (docs).

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:review [prd | design | plan | docs | all]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `prd | design | plan | docs | all` | what to review |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:review prd`: score the PRD and revise until it passes

**Produces:** .dev/reviews/<target>/report.md and scores

**Related:** [`prd`](#prd), [`plan`](#plan), [`docs`](#docs)

### autopilot

Drives the build on its own: conception and planning, then milestone after milestone and the next release, until the project is stable; pauses follow your autonomy settings.

**When:** After the interview, when you want the app built with minimal interaction (also overnight).

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:autopilot [--until prd|architecture|design|plan|qa|usability|docs|release] [--milestone M1] [--milestones N] [--board]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--until step` | stop at a step: prd, architecture, design, plan, qa, usability, docs or release (e.g. plan, to review the documents first) |
| `--milestone M1` | build only one milestone |
| `--milestones N` | stop after N approved gates, to resume in a fresh session (cheaper long runs) |
| `--board` | how the board's Autopilot switch runs it: headless, questions go to Needs you, ends saying why (you do not type it) |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:autopilot`: build everything
- `/dev-kit:autopilot --until plan`: only the documents, so you can review them
- `/dev-kit:autopilot --milestone M1`: one milestone, e.g. to gauge cost
- `/dev-kit:autopilot --milestones 2`: two milestones, then resume in a new session

**Produces:** everything below, one commit per task

**Related:** [`status`](#status), [`backlog`](#backlog), [`costs`](#costs)

### implement

Implements ready tasks test-first, full suite, one commit per task; hotfix lane first.

**When:** To build tasks by hand instead of autopilot, or to run a specific task (e.g. a fix).

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:implement [T-003 | --tasks N | --milestone M1 | --parallel N | --skip-gate | --round-child]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `T-003` | one task |
| `--milestone M1 | --tasks N` | a milestone or N tasks |
| `--parallel N` | N isolated implementers in git worktrees |
| `--skip-gate` | work past a pending gate (records an ADR and sets the gate skipped) |
| `--round-child` | internal: the milestone runs in a child session started by `dev_state.py round run` |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:implement T-031`: build one task (e.g. a hotfix)
- `/dev-kit:implement --milestone M2 --parallel 3`: build M2 with 3 workers

**Produces:** code, tests, one commit per task

**Related:** [`test`](#test), [`qa`](#qa), [`issue`](#issue)

### test

Test strategy and test writing: plan, missing tests for a task or path, flaky tests.

**When:** Tests are missing, failing or flaky, or you want to define the testing approach.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:test [T-003 | path | 'plan' | 'fix-flaky']`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `T-003 | path` | cover a task or a folder |
| `plan` | write the test plan |
| `fix-flaky` | find and fix flaky tests |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:test src/auth`: add missing tests for a folder

**Produces:** .dev/qa/test-plan.md, tests

**Related:** [`implement`](#implement), [`qa`](#qa)

### qa

Milestone gate: auditors in parallel, 0-100 score per dimension, fix tasks until the cut-off is met.

**When:** When a milestone's tasks are done, or to check one task (e.g. after a hotfix).

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:qa [M1 | --only code,security,tests,spec,data,deps,ops,perf,a11y,visual,copy | --scope T-003 | --full | --round-child]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `M1` | gate of a milestone |
| `--scope T-003` | audit one task |
| `--only code,security,...` | run a subset of auditors |
| `--full` | audit everything again, without reusing earlier clean reviews |
| `--round-child` | internal: one round in a child session started by `dev_state.py round run` |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:qa M2`: gate M2
- `/dev-kit:qa --scope T-031`: check a hotfix

**Produces:** .dev/qa/<M>/report.md, scores, fix tasks

**Related:** [`implement`](#implement), [`issue`](#issue), [`usability`](#usability)

### usability

Whole-product audit of usability, accessibility, visuals and copy, with score and fix tasks.

**When:** After the UI milestones are built, before release.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:usability [screen ids | flow ids | --url http://localhost:3000]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `screens or flows` | limit the audit |
| `--url` | audit a running app |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:usability`: audit every screen

**Produces:** .dev/qa/ux/report.md, screenshots, fix tasks

**Related:** [`qa`](#qa), [`issue`](#issue)

### issue

Report a bug, improvement or scope change in plain words; the kit classifies and routes it without breaking the milestone cadence.

**When:** You found a bug or want something to work differently, during or after the build.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:issue ["description" | I-003 | --from F-012 M3 | --schedule I-003 M8 | --close I-003 wontfix|duplicate]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"description"` | new issue |
| `I-003` | show or update |
| `--from F-012 M3` | promote a deferred QA finding |
| `--schedule I-003 M8` | bring into an existing milestone |
| `--close I-003 wontfix | duplicate I-001` | close (as duplicate of another issue) |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:issue "the Save button on the profile page does nothing"`: report a bug
- `/dev-kit:issue "export reports as CSV"`: request a change
- `/dev-kit:issue --from F-012 M3`: turn a deferred finding into an issue

**Produces:** .dev/issues.md, tasks linked to the issue

**Related:** [`backlog`](#backlog), [`implement`](#implement), [`plan`](#plan)

### backlog

Everything pending: hotfix, issue queue, next buffer, tasks, parked questions, deferred findings, deploys.

**When:** You want to know what is left or what to do next.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:backlog [issues | tasks | questions | findings | deploy]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `issues | tasks | questions | findings | deploy` | one section only |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:backlog`: the full list and the recommended next step
- `/dev-kit:backlog issues`: only issues

**Produces:** nothing (read-only)

**Related:** [`issue`](#issue), [`status`](#status), [`interview`](#interview)

### settings

Shows and changes the project's settings in plain words: autonomy, quality bar, rounds, reuse, checks, deploys, tips, status line and notifications.

**When:** You want the kit more or less autonomous or strict, to turn something on or off, or to see the configuration.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:settings [show | <what to change, in words> | tips off|on|always|reset | status line | notifications]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `show` | current settings and their effect |
| `<what to change, in words>` | e.g. "run overnight", "stricter gates", "no tips" |
| `tips off|on|always|reset` | tips; reset shows them again |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:settings`: see how the kit is configured
- `/dev-kit:settings run overnight without asking`: unattended level with the floors kept
- `/dev-kit:settings tips off`: no more tips

**Produces:** the changed setting in .dev/state.json and an ADR for decisions

**Related:** [`interview`](#interview), [`status`](#status), [`help`](#help)

### deploy

Production deploy of an approved milestone or release: preflight, backup, dry-run, install, migrations, smoke checks.

**When:** After a gate when the project deploys per milestone, at release, or to check how far production is behind.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:deploy [M3 | --check | --dry-run | --health | --rollback R2]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `M3` | deploy a milestone |
| `--check` | only show the drift |
| `--dry-run` | preflight and the method's own dry-run; nothing installed or recorded |
| `--health` | run the production health check now, and offer to schedule it |
| `--rollback R2` | turn the release flag of R2 off in production (release flags on) |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:deploy --check`: is production up to date?
- `/dev-kit:deploy --health`: is production healthy?
- `/dev-kit:deploy M4`: deploy M4

**Produces:** deploy record shown by status; the health check result (.dev/run/prod-health.json) and, on failure, one expedite issue

**Related:** [`release`](#release), [`status`](#status)

### docs

Project documentation from the artifacts and code: README, user guide, API reference, CHANGELOG.

**When:** Before a release, or when you need docs for the project.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:docs [readme | guide | api | changelog | all]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `readme | guide | api | changelog | all` | what to write |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:docs all`: all project docs

**Produces:** README.md, docs/, CHANGELOG.md

**Related:** [`review`](#review), [`release`](#release)

### release

Ships the next release (the milestones closed since the last release, or the next planned release): audits, the release review and your approve/reject decision for a planned release, then version, CHANGELOG, tag, production deploy and the release record; patch releases for hotfixes.

**When:** Between milestones, when closed milestones wait for the next release or a planned release has all its milestones closed (the board and status show it), to approve or reject a release waiting for you, or after a hotfix.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:release [version e.g. 1.0.0 | --dry-run | --hotfix | --approve | --reject "feedback"]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `version` | explicit version |
| `--dry-run` | check without changing anything |
| `--hotfix` | patch release for a closed hotfix |
| `--approve` | approve the planned release waiting for you |
| `--reject "feedback"` | reject it; each line of feedback becomes a fix task |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:release`: check, audit and submit the next planned release for your approval (or decide on the one waiting)
- `/dev-kit:release --reject "the error message on duplicate email is unclear"`: send the release back with what must change
- `/dev-kit:release --dry-run`: see what would happen
- `/dev-kit:release --hotfix`: ship a hotfix as a patch version

**Produces:** version bump, release notes, tag, release record (nothing waits any more; with nothing open the project is stable)

**Related:** [`deploy`](#deploy), [`docs`](#docs)

### costs

Token usage and estimated US$ (API-equivalent) per stage, agent, model or session; CSV of tokens.

**When:** You want to know how much was spent and where.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:costs [--all | --since YYYY-MM-DD] [--by stage|agent|model|session|milestone] [--csv] [--time]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--all | --since YYYY-MM-DD` | period (default: current session) |
| `--by stage|agent|model|session|milestone` | grouping |
| `--csv` | export every token count |
| `--time` | time per agent and skill, and what the work ledger reused |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:costs`: cost of this session by stage
- `/dev-kit:costs --all --by agent --csv`: whole project by agent, with CSV
- `/dev-kit:costs --time --all`: where the time went, and how much rework was avoided

**Produces:** .dev/costs/ (usage, prices, CSV)

**Related:** [`feedback`](#feedback), [`status`](#status)

### feedback

Evaluation of the session: grade per stage with reasons, what worked and failed, suggestions for the kit.

**When:** After a run, to review it or to send feedback to the dev-kit author.

**Usage:** `/dev-kit:feedback [--all | --since YYYY-MM-DD]`

| Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--all | --since YYYY-MM-DD` | period (default: current session) |

**Examples:**

- `/dev-kit:feedback`: evaluate this session

**Produces:** .dev/feedback/feedback-report-<timestamp>.md and export

**Related:** [`costs`](#costs)
